title: A tiny env and args tool
description:
Write a small command-line tool in assembly that works with its arguments and environment.

```
$ ./tool count
3 arguments, 24 environment variables
$ ./tool get HOME
/home/ada
$ ./tool sum 10 20 -5
25
$ ./tool
usage: tool count | get NAME | sum NUMBERS...   (on standard error, exit code 2)
```

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .text
_start:
        mov     rdi, [rsp]
        call    print_int
        call    print_newline
        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: Keep `argc` and the address of `argv[0]` in callee-saved registers before calling anything, since calls change `rsp` (lesson 8.05).
Compare the command word with each name using a `starts_with`-style routine that also checks the zero at the end.
requirements: Read `argc`, `argv` and the environment from the stack at `_start`.
Three commands; anything else prints the usage to standard error and exits with code 2.
Numbers parsed and checked; a bad number exits with code 1 and a message.
stretch: Add `set NAME=value` that runs another program with the changed environment using the `execve` system call.
